data.name: Subject 13
data.detailed_description:
Subject 13 is the new adventure game developed by Paul Cuisset—the man behind "Flashback", "Future Wars: Adventures in Time" and "Moto Racer"—in partnership with Microïds.

This is a true adventure game. It depicts a mysterious universe filled with secret hiding places and all kinds of mechanisms that the player discovers, analyzes, and activates. There are also objects to collect and to figure out how to use in the backdrops…

Subject 13 will make you travel from a secret base that has been abandoned to a strange and mysterious island, so you can discover the real story. You'll have to muster all your insight and intelligence for this daunting challenge.

Key Features

  • Stunning 3D rendering
  • Intuitive interface
  • Progressive difficulty
  • Quality dubbing

data.short_description: Play as Franklin Fargo, a quiet physics professor who has led a bitter existence ever since his fiancée died in a holdup in which he was supposed to be the victim. One morning, he wakes up in the middle of an abandoned scientific facility. His only link with the outside world is a voice that calls him "Subject 13".

reviews.review:
[b]My Playtime:[/b] 4.5h (100% achievement, finished the game)
[b]Grindy Achievement(s):[/b] No.
[b]Optional Achievement(s):[/b] Yes (4 achievements).
[b]Difficult Achievement(s):[/b] Yes (1 achievement where you need to finish Minesweeper in 10 minutes)

[h1]Intro[/h1]
[i]Subject 13[/i] is a point-and-click game with some puzzles and minigames in it. The puzzles are designed in a simpler version of [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/288160/The_Room/][i]The Room[/i][/url] ([url=https://steamcommunity.com/profiles/76561198132503739/recommended/288160]my review[/url]), where you can move objects around to figure out what you can do with them.

[b]Pros:[/b]
- Different puzzles and minigames to solve
- Voice-overs in all dialogues

[b]Cons:[/b]
- Solutions tend not to make any sense
- The rotatable puzzles are not intuitive enough

[b]Specs[/b]
AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D, 16GB RAM, AMD Radeon RX 9060 XT

[h1]Should you buy this game?[/h1]
[i]The combination of point-and-click and simple puzzles might work here if not for the weird solutions that force you to look up some guides to solve.[/i]

[hr][/hr]
[h1]In-Depth Review[/h1]

[h3]The Game[/h3]
[b]Gameplay[/b]
[i]Subject 13[/i] is a point-and-click game where you play as Franklin, who is stranded on an island with no memory. Guided by a mysterious voice that keeps calling him Subject 13, he goes on a journey that tests his problem-solving skills to reach where the mysterious voice is located.

The game takes place in an area where you can pick some objects to use or combine with other objects, similar to other point-and-click games. Unlike other games in this genre, some objects will be interactable, allowing you to move parts of them to reveal certain items. I like these kinds of puzzles since they remind me of [i]The Room[/i], albeit simpler. However, these mechanics tend to be not intuitive, causing confusion on what to do to progress at times.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2817259482 

The solutions to the point-and-click puzzles tend to not make any sense. You often need to think outside the box to figure out what to do to proceed, without even knowing what the problem is that you need to solve. Not to mention, the solution will require multiple steps involving multiple items, which won't even cross your mind unless you already know what to do.

Other than that, the game behaves similarly to other point-and-click games, with it dividing itself into the point-and-click puzzles where you need to use or combine items, and minigames. The minigames are mostly block puzzles where you need to move a certain block that is surrounded by other blocks, although there are other puzzles like Minesweeper as well. They are usually minigames that you are already familiar with, with some altered mechanics. This makes it easier to figure out what to do with them.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2835220179 

Despite the high resolution option, the game still looks aged. The character's body and background look blocky, and the animation looks stiff. The story, which starts as a mystery, becomes a comedy due to the same reason. That being said, the ending is just weird compared to the mystery it gives at the beginning, plus it doesn't really conclude the story well.

[b]Length and Difficulty[/b]
I finished the game in 4.5h. I spent like 1 hour to finish the last puzzle to get an achievement by finishing it within 10 minutes. It might be hard to figure out what to do to progress the game at times, although there is a hint button to help with that, along with a skip button to skip the minigames that you are having difficulty with.

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
While it offers some interesting puzzle mechanics, the puzzles either don't make any sense or aren't intuitive enough to deduce. You'll be stuck reading guides to find where you need to go and what to do next. The voiceover and the lore might be nice, but it's not enough to keep you invested. Plus, the ending doesn't seem to be worth it for the journey it offers, save for the laugh due to the aged animation. I don't think I could recommend playing this.
